title: Trig identities
goal: I can simplify expressions and prove identities.
teach: Two identities hold for every angle: tan x = sin xcos x and sin² x + cos² x = 1 (so 1 − cos² x = sin² x and 1 − sin² x = cos² x). To prove an identity, start with the more complicated side and simplify it until it equals the other side.
tvis:
Prove1 − cos² xsin x cos x = tan x
Left sidesin² xsin x cos x
Cancel sin xsin xcos x
= right sidetan x

ex.q: Prove that 1 − cos² xsin x cos x = tan x.
steps: Left side: 1 − cos² x = sin² x, so we get sin² xsin x cos x.
Cancel sin x: sin xcos x.

watch: 1 − cos x is not sin x. The identity uses squares: 1 − cos² x = sin² x.

qs.text: sin x = 0,6 and x is acute. Find cos x without finding x.
qs.steps:
1. Identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 and tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ.
2. cos²x = 1 − sin²x = 1 − 0,36 = 0,64
3. x is acute, so cos x is positive: cos x = √0,64 = 0,8
